cells.value: The tailnet policy file as saved in Alex's admin console: policy v4, least privilege, saved by Alex on 2026-10-03 00:15:55Z (it replaced the 2026-10-01 allow-all file), what each part does, how it was checked, and a copy-ready file for a new tailnet. It closes retest gap G09 with Rebuild from zero steps 6.0 to 6.6. Saving a policy is the owner's: an agent gives the text and the steps. Facts from the network-rules job (work/2026-10-02_network-rules/notes/network-rules.md); the 2026-10-01 file is in play spp-p20b's notes (notes/gap-facts-infra.md §3). Built by work/2026-10-01_setup-playbook/build_tabs.py from tabs/tailscale-policy.json; never edit this tab by hand.
1. The policy file as saved (v4, 110 lines, sha256 e49d6625…; saved by Alex 2026-10-03 00:15:55Z, ETag 79591c0d… → f271330f…; 9/9 after-save checks)
"hosts": 12 aliases (javante, javar-orgo, Alex's MacBook and iPhone with IPv6 twins, the hub and the 5 agents)

Names for fixed tailnet addresses, so a rule or test can name one machine without retagging. Grants use only javante and javar-orgo; the 6 ephemeral Orgo machines appear only in deny tests, so a stale address blocks nothing.
"grants": alex@ → * (all ports); tag:server → autogroup:internet; javar-orgo → javante tcp:9900; javante → javar-orgo tcp:18881 and tcp:9999

Least privilege: Alex's devices reach everything; every Orgo machine reaches only the internet through the home exit node; Javar → Javante A2A; Javante → Javar's GHL bridge and the fallback file push (9999 is Alex's call). Everything else is blocked.

After the save: Javar and Javante answer on 443 from the MacBook; the exit node shows Comcast from all 7 Orgo machines; Javar's A2A card 200; the Mac mini reaches 18881; b2b → javante:9900 now fails (checks 2, 4-7).
"ssh": accept alex@ → tag:server (root or any user); check autogroup:member → autogroup:self
Only Alex may SSH into the Orgo machines (agents can't SSH into each other, and agent@ can't); the default check rule stays for each person's own devices.
tailscale ssh root@b2b-sales-agent rc 0, and all 6 SSH-reachable Orgo machines answered (check 3).
Defines tag:server. Admins as before, plus Alex by name, so he keeps the label after agent@ becomes a Member (one deliberate, additive change; today's exact line also validates).
Kept in the live policy (check 1: the parsed live JSON equals v4).
No nodeAttrs: Funnel is no longer granted.
No machine may publish a service to the internet through Funnel.
No machine used Funnel (checked 2026-10-02 on the MacBook, javante, javar-orgo and the other six Orgo machines).
Checks Tailscale runs on every save: the allowed flows pass and named leaks are refused, by identity and by address (IPv6 too). If one fails, the console refuses to save.
Validation 2026-10-03 00:06:48Z returned {} (all pass); 4 planted leaks on v4 were each rejected (network-rules §7).
2. Copy-ready policy for a new tailnet (policy v4; swap alex@ for your own login, <agent login> for your agent's, and the host addresses for your machines')

Admin console > Access controls > JSON editor: paste it, change the names and addresses, Save (Tailscale runs the tests first and refuses a failing file). Rollback: paste the previous file (work/2026-10-02_network-rules/2026-10-02_rollback-policy.hujson). Saving is the owner's: a security setting.
Whether Device approval is on in Alex's tailnet (it decides the Pre-approved tick).
The chosen expiry of the saved auth key (at most 90 days).
That SSH into the hub is refused: taken from Tailscale's shields-up documentation, not tested.
Why the exit-node Mac mini carries a 'suggest-exit-node' capability: no policy line sets it.
javante (the Mac mini) is still shared with Kanwal Singh's outside account; the policy blocks it, and revoking the share is Alex's click (Machines > Filters > Shared > Shared by me > javante).
